paper.title: Autonomous metabolic reprogramming and oxidative stress characterize endothelial dysfunction in acute myocardial infarction
paper.abstract: Compelling evidence has accumulated on the role of oxidative stress on the endothelial cell (EC) dysfunction in acute coronary syndrome. Unveiling the underlying metabolic determinants has been hampered by the scarcity of appropriate cell models to address cell-autonomous mechanisms of EC dysfunction. We have generated endothelial cells derived from thrombectomy specimens from patients affected with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and conducted phenotypical and metabolic characterizations. AMI-derived endothelial cells (AMIECs) display impaired growth, migration, and tubulogenesis. Metabolically, AMIECs displayed augmented ROS and glutathione intracellular content, with a diminished glucose consumption coupled to high lactate production. In AMIECs, while PFKFB3 protein levels of were downregulated, PFKFB4 levels were upregulated, suggesting a shunting of glycolysis towards the pentose phosphate pathway, supported by upregulation of G6PD. Furthermore, the glutaminolytic enzyme GLS was upregulated in AMIECs, providing an explanation for the increase in glutathione content. Finally, AMIECs displayed a significantly higher mitochondrial membrane potential than control ECs, which, together with high ROS levels, suggests a coupled mitochondrial activity. We suggest that high mitochondrial proton coupling underlies the high production of ROS, balanced by PPP- and glutaminolysis-driven synthesis of glutathione, as a primary, cell-autonomous abnormality driving EC dysfunction in AMI.

nodes.label: AMI patient-derived coronary endothelial cells (AMIECs) exhibit pharmacologicall…
nodes.claim: AMI patient-derived coronary endothelial cells (AMIECs) exhibit pharmacologically actionable cell-autonomous metabolic dysfunction, characterized by a shift from glycolysis toward glutaminolysis and pentose phosphate pathway activation, driven by mitochondrial hyperpolarization and excess ROS production.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Our observations point to pharmacologically actionable cell-autonomous metabolic dysfunction in these cells.

strengths: The paper presents a coherent narrative linking multiple metabolic observations (low glycolysis, high glutaminolysis, PPP activation, mitochondrial hyperpolarization, elevated ROS) into an integrated model of metabolic dysfunction.
Multiple independent lines of evidence are presented across 8 patient-derived cell lines, providing some degree of biological replication.
The cell-autonomous nature of the dysfunction is supported by the in vitro setting where environmental variables are controlled.
weaknesses: The claim of 'pharmacologically actionable' dysfunction is entirely speculative — no pharmacological intervention (e.g., uncoupling agents) was actually tested on AMIECs in this study.

The use of a single commercial HCAEC line as the sole control is a critical limitation; inter-individual variation in healthy coronary ECs is uncharacterized, making it impossible to distinguish disease-specific from individual variation.

No direct measurement of glycolytic flux, mitochondrial respiration (e.g., Seahorse assays), or oxidative phosphorylation rates was performed. The metabolic model is built almost entirely from indirect proxies (protein expression, metabolite levels in media).
No isotope tracing experiments were conducted to demonstrate the proposed carbon flux from glutamine to lactate or through the PPP, which are central mechanistic assertions.
Sample size is small (n=8 patients) and no matching of patient demographics/comorbidities with control cell donors is described.
The root claim conflates observed correlative metabolic differences with a causally 'driven' mechanism — no causal evidence is provided.
alternative_interpretations: The metabolic differences may reflect selection bias during the isolation and culture process from thrombectomy specimens, rather than genuine cell-autonomous properties of coronary ECs in AMI patients.
Differences may reflect inter-individual genetic variation rather than disease-associated metabolic reprogramming, given only one control cell line was used.
The metabolic phenotype could represent culture adaptation of cells from an ischemic environment rather than a stable, pharmacologically targetable dysfunction.
required_assumptions: A single commercial HCAEC line is representative of healthy coronary endothelial cell metabolism.
In vitro metabolic phenotypes faithfully reflect in vivo endothelial dysfunction in AMI patients.
The observed metabolic alterations are causally linked rather than merely correlated.
Protein expression levels reliably predict metabolic flux through the respective pathways.
The proposed pharmacological intervention (uncoupling) would actually reverse the phenotype.
evaluation.notes: The term 'pharmacologically actionable' in this root claim is unsupported by any experimental pharmacological data in the paper. This is a significant overstatement relative to the evidence provided.

nodes.label: AMIECs are bona fide endothelial cells that are dysfunctional in major cell-auto…
nodes.claim: AMIECs are bona fide endothelial cells that are dysfunctional in major cell-autonomous processes, namely proliferation, migration, and tubulogenesis.
nodes.verbatim_quote: These results indicate that AMI patient-derived coronary endothelial cells are dysfunctional in major cell-autonomous processes, namely growth and migration.

strengths: Endothelial identity is confirmed by multiple markers (V-CAM1, PECAM-1, CD-34, CD-105) via Western blotting.
Functional assays (growth curves, wound healing, tubulogenesis) all consistently show impairment across multiple patient-derived lines.
Migration assays were performed with mitomycin C to separate migration from proliferation effects.
weaknesses: Western blotting for endothelial markers is shown but no quantification or comparison of expression levels between AMIECs and HCAECs is provided — it is unclear whether marker expression levels are equivalent.
No flow cytometric quantification of endothelial markers or negative selection against non-endothelial contaminants (e.g., smooth muscle cells, fibroblasts) was performed to ensure culture purity.
Growth curves use n=3 technical replicates, not biological replicates from independent experiments.

Cell cycle analysis at a single time point (24 hr) is insufficient to characterize proliferative dynamics; the claim of 'overall slowing affecting all phases equally' is not well-supported by a single snapshot.
The control is a single commercial cell line, making it impossible to assess normal variation in these functional assays.
alternative_interpretations: The slow growth and impaired migration could reflect cellular senescence or culture-induced stress from the isolation procedure rather than intrinsic dysfunction.
Thrombectomy-derived cells may include a heterogeneous population, and subpopulations of non-endothelial or damaged cells could skew functional assays.
Passage number differences between AMIECs and HCAECs could account for functional differences.
required_assumptions: The isolation procedure yields pure endothelial cell populations.
A single HCAEC control line provides an appropriate baseline for multiple patient-derived lines.
In vitro functional assays (growth, migration, tubulogenesis) are valid readouts of in vivo endothelial function.
evaluation.notes: The figure legend mentions CD-10 rather than CD-105 in panel B, suggesting possible typographical errors that could reflect carelessness in manuscript preparation.

nodes.label: AMIECs display diminished glycolysis compared to normal coronary endothelial cel…
nodes.claim: AMIECs display diminished glycolysis compared to normal coronary endothelial cells, as evidenced by low glucose consumption and PFKFB3 downregulation.
nodes.verbatim_quote: AMIECs display low levels of glycolysis, as attested by low glucose consumption and downregulation of PFKFB3

strengths: Glucose consumption measurements in 6/8 AMIECs show significantly lower rates than controls, which is internally consistent with lower PFKFB3 expression.
PFKFB3 downregulation is demonstrated by Western blotting in 7/8 lines with quantification from triplicate experiments.
CE-45 serves as an internal positive control — it has near-normal PFKFB3 and higher glucose consumption, strengthening the PFKFB3-glucose uptake association.
weaknesses: No direct measurement of glycolytic flux was performed (e.g., 13C-glucose tracing, Seahorse glycolysis stress test). Glucose consumption from media is a crude proxy that does not distinguish glycolysis from PPP or other glucose-consuming pathways.
Two of 8 AMIECs (CE-45 and CE-61) actually consume MORE glucose than controls, directly contradicting the general claim of 'diminished glycolysis.' The claim requires qualification.
PFKFB3 protein levels do not necessarily reflect enzyme activity; no PFKFB3 activity assay was performed.
No measurement of fructose-2,6-bisphosphate (F2,6BP) levels was made, which would be the direct functional readout of PFKFB3 activity.
Glucose transporter expression was not examined.
alternative_interpretations: Lower glucose consumption could reflect lower cellular metabolic demand due to slower growth rather than a primary glycolytic defect.
PFKFB3 downregulation could be a consequence rather than a cause of reduced glucose uptake.
required_assumptions: Glucose consumption from media reliably reflects glycolytic flux.
PFKFB3 protein levels are a valid proxy for glycolytic capacity.
The two outlier cell lines (CE-45, CE-61) do not invalidate the general conclusion.
evaluation.notes: The claim is presented as a general feature of AMIECs, but 2/8 lines are clear exceptions. The authors acknowledge this but still frame the claim broadly.

nodes.label: AMIECs undergo a switch in carbon source preference from glucose to glutamine, w…
nodes.claim: AMIECs undergo a switch in carbon source preference from glucose to glutamine, with enhanced glutaminolysis serving both as an alternative energy source and as a means to maintain redox homeostasis.
nodes.verbatim_quote: a switch in carbon source preference from glucose to glutamine, possibly as an adaptive mechanism aimed at potentiating the production of glutathione, while employing alternative pyruvate-to-lactate conversion pathways that replenish NAD+

strengths: Glutamine consumption is measurably higher in AMIECs, and the glutamine-to-glucose ratio is substantially greater.
GLS1 isoform upregulation (both KGA and GAC) is consistent with enhanced glutaminolysis.
The narrative connecting glutamine to lactate production via the malic enzyme pathway is biochemically plausible.
weaknesses: No isotope tracing (13C-glutamine) was performed to demonstrate that glutamine is actually being used as a carbon source for the TCA cycle or for lactate production. This is the single most critical experiment missing from this paper.
No direct measurement of TCA cycle flux from glutamine-derived carbons was performed. GC/MS analysis of TCA intermediates was mentioned but results are not shown in the text.
No measurement of malic enzyme expression or activity was performed, despite the claim that glutamine-derived lactate production occurs via the malic enzyme pathway.
LDH-A expression/activity was not measured.
The claim that glutamine is the 'main carbon source' is extremely strong given only indirect evidence (consumption ratios and enzyme expression levels).
Oxygen consumption rate measurements are absent, which would directly test whether mitochondrial glutamine oxidation is occurring.
alternative_interpretations: Higher glutamine consumption could primarily serve biosynthetic roles (amino acid, nucleotide synthesis) rather than bioenergetic carbon source replacement.
The higher glutamine consumption may primarily drive glutathione synthesis rather than TCA cycle anaplerosis.
Lactate could be produced from sources other than glutamine — e.g., amino acid catabolism from the rich culture medium.
required_assumptions: Glutamine consumption rate reflects its use as a primary carbon source rather than for biosynthetic purposes.
The malic enzyme pathway is active and produces significant lactate from glutamine-derived intermediates.
The biochemical pathway proposed (glutamine → glutamate → α-KG → malate → pyruvate → lactate) is operational in these cells.
evaluation.notes: This is perhaps the most ambitious claim in the paper and simultaneously the least well-supported experimentally. Isotope tracing is now standard methodology for such claims and its absence is a major gap.

nodes.label: AMIECs show mitochondrial hyperpolarization indicating increased mitochondrial a…
nodes.claim: AMIECs show mitochondrial hyperpolarization indicating increased mitochondrial activity, which is a likely source of their excess ROS production.
nodes.verbatim_quote: The combination of high membrane potential and high ROS levels suggests robust proton coupling at the inner mitochondrial membrane

strengths: DiIC1(5) data consistently shows higher mitochondrial membrane potential across all 8 AMIEC lines.
CCCP control confirms that the DiIC1(5) signal is mitochondrial-membrane-potential-dependent.
The co-occurrence of high membrane potential with high ROS is biologically coherent, as hyperpolarized mitochondria are known to produce more ROS.
weaknesses: DiIC1(5) is a single-dye assay susceptible to artifacts from differences in mitochondrial mass, cell size, or plasma membrane potential. No normalization for mitochondrial mass (e.g., MitoTracker Green or citrate synthase activity) was performed.

No direct measurement of mitochondrial respiration was made (e.g., Seahorse OCR measurements). High membrane potential does not necessarily equal high mitochondrial activity — it could reflect impaired ATP synthase function or reduced ATP demand.

The causal claim that mitochondrial hyperpolarization is the 'likely source' of excess ROS is not tested. ROS could come from NOX enzymes, as the authors themselves acknowledge, but this alternative was not experimentally explored.
No measurement of mitochondrial superoxide specifically (e.g., MitoSOX) was performed — H2DCFDA measures total cellular ROS, not specifically mitochondrial ROS.
No assessment of mitochondrial morphology, dynamics, or respiratory chain complex expression/activity was performed.
alternative_interpretations: High membrane potential could reflect reduced ATP synthase activity or low ATP demand rather than increased electron transport chain activity.
ROS may originate primarily from NAD(P)H oxidases or other cytoplasmic sources rather than mitochondria.
Mitochondrial hyperpolarization could be a compensatory response to other cellular stresses rather than a primary defect.
required_assumptions: DiIC1(5) fluorescence accurately reflects mitochondrial membrane potential without confounding by mitochondrial mass differences.
High membrane potential implies high mitochondrial respiratory activity.
Mitochondria are the primary source of excess ROS in AMIECs.
evaluation.notes: The link between mitochondrial hyperpolarization and ROS is correlative only. Causation would require showing that uncoupling reduces ROS in these specific cells, which was not done.

nodes.label: AMIECs activate compensatory redox homeostasis mechanisms, including a glycolysi…
nodes.claim: AMIECs activate compensatory redox homeostasis mechanisms, including a glycolysis-to-PPP shunt and upregulated glutathione biosynthesis, to counter excess ROS.
nodes.verbatim_quote: a strong proton coupling in the mitochondrial membrane that results in excess ROS production, countered by enhanced NADPH and glutathione levels, driven by a glycolysis-to-PPP shunt and an enhanced glutamine metabolism

strengths: Multiple lines of evidence converge: high G6PD expression and activity, high PFKFB4 expression, high ROS, high glutathione — all consistent with the PPP shunt and compensatory redox homeostasis narrative.
Both protein levels and enzyme activity were measured for G6PD, strengthening the evidence for PPP activation.
The observation that CE-45 is a consistent outlier across multiple measurements (near-normal G6PD, near-normal ROS, near-normal PFKFB3) provides internal validation.
weaknesses: No direct measurement of PPP flux was performed (e.g., 1-14C/6-14C glucose ratio or 13C-glucose tracing into PPP products).
NADPH levels were not directly measured — the claim of enhanced NADPH production is entirely inferred.
The relationship between high PFKFB4 and PPP shunting is mechanistically indirect and relies on literature from cancer cells that may not translate to endothelial cells.
No measurement of ribose-5-phosphate or nucleotide levels was reported to confirm non-oxidative PPP branch activation.
The logical chain from 'high PFKFB4 + low PFKFB3 → glycolysis-to-PPP shunt' is plausible but not demonstrated directly.
alternative_interpretations: High G6PD could be a general stress response rather than specifically indicating a glycolysis-to-PPP shunt.
High glutathione levels could be maintained through increased cystine import (xCT transporter) rather than increased PPP-derived NADPH.
ROS elevation and glutathione upregulation could be independent of PPP activation.
required_assumptions: G6PD expression and activity levels reliably indicate PPP flux.
The PFKFB3/PFKFB4 ratio determines glucose-6-phosphate partitioning between glycolysis and PPP.
High glutathione levels are maintained primarily through NADPH from the PPP.
evaluation.notes: This claim is among the better-supported in the paper because multiple independent measurements converge, but the lack of direct flux measurements remains a significant limitation.

nodes.label: The metabolic dysfunction in AMIECs involves two primary cell-autonomous deficie…
nodes.claim: The metabolic dysfunction in AMIECs involves two primary cell-autonomous deficiencies that are pharmacologically actionable through mitochondrial uncoupling.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Independent of the original insult, a possible intervention to revert the observed mitochondrial dysfunction would be the use of pharmacological uncouplers to mitigate ROS production and the accompanying metabolic reprogramming

strengths: The two-deficiency model provides a parsimonious explanation for the ensemble of observations.
The suggestion of pharmacological uncouplers is grounded in the literature on mitochondrial uncoupling and ROS.
weaknesses: No pharmacological uncoupler experiment was performed in this study. The claim of 'pharmacologically actionable' dysfunction is pure speculation without any rescue experiment.
No genetic manipulation (e.g., PFKFB3 overexpression, GLS1 knockdown, UCP expression) was performed to test causality of any proposed mechanism.
The designation of these as 'primary deficiencies' implies causality that has not been established — the observations are all correlative.
The paper does not distinguish whether these are truly two independent primary deficiencies or a single deficiency with downstream consequences.
No in vivo validation or clinical correlation was performed.
alternative_interpretations: The metabolic phenotype could be a secondary adaptation to the isolation and culture conditions rather than a primary deficiency.
Uncoupling could potentially harm cells by reducing ATP production, and the net effect might not be beneficial.
The observed phenotypes could reflect a single upstream cause (e.g., epigenetic reprogramming) rather than two independent primary deficiencies.
required_assumptions: The metabolic phenotype observed in vitro represents a stable, pharmacologically targetable state.
Mitochondrial uncoupling would reverse the entire cascade of metabolic reprogramming.
The two deficiencies are truly 'primary' rather than secondary to a common upstream cause.
Results from animal models of UCP1 knockout are translatable to human AMI endothelial cells.
evaluation.notes: This claim epitomizes the gap between the observational data presented and the therapeutic implications suggested. Without any intervention experiment, the 'pharmacologically actionable' framing is premature.

nodes.label: AMIECs are confirmed as endothelial cells by expression of canonical endothelial…
nodes.claim: AMIECs are confirmed as endothelial cells by expression of canonical endothelial markers and by morphological appearance similar to control HCAECs.
nodes.verbatim_quote: The endothelial nature of these cells was confirmed by Western blotting for the expression of the endothelial markers, V-CAM1, PECAM-1, CD-34, and CD-105

strengths: Four canonical endothelial markers (V-CAM1, PECAM-1, CD-34, CD-105) were used for identification.
Morphological assessment under bright field imaging provides additional supporting evidence.
weaknesses: Western blotting is shown as representative images without quantification comparing expression levels between AMIECs and HCAECs.
No negative markers (e.g., smooth muscle actin, fibroblast markers) were tested to rule out contaminating cell populations.
No flow cytometry for surface marker quantification was performed — this would provide more rigorous cell-by-cell characterization.
V-CAM1 is upregulated by inflammation and its presence could reflect activated rather than normal endothelial identity.
alternative_interpretations: Expression of endothelial markers does not rule out partial endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, which could confound functional assays.
Marker expression confirms lineage but not functional endothelial competence.
required_assumptions: These four markers are sufficient to confirm endothelial identity and exclude contaminating cell types.
Western blotting is adequate for cell identity confirmation.
evaluation.notes: The figure legend mentions CD-10 instead of CD-105 in panel B, raising concerns about attention to detail.

nodes.label: All AMIECs consistently display slower growth rates compared to control HCAECs, …
nodes.claim: All AMIECs consistently display slower growth rates compared to control HCAECs, with an overall slowing down of growth affecting all phases of the cell cycle equally.
nodes.verbatim_quote: all AMIECs consistently displayed slower growth rates as compared to control HCAECs

strengths: Growth curves over 168 hr provide time-course data showing consistent slower growth across all 8 AMIEC lines.
Cell cycle analysis was performed to investigate the mechanism underlying slower growth.
weaknesses: The claim that growth slowing 'affects all phases equally' is based on a single-timepoint cell cycle analysis (24 hr) showing no significant differences, which is insufficient evidence for such a claim.
n=3 is stated but it is unclear whether these are biological or technical replicates.
Only one control cell line was used; inter-individual variation in healthy coronary EC growth rates is unknown.
No assessment of apoptosis or senescence markers was performed, which could contribute to apparent slower growth.
Passage numbers of AMIECs vs. HCAECs are not reported — this is critical for growth rate comparisons.
alternative_interpretations: Slower growth could reflect replicative senescence or stress-induced growth arrest rather than a disease-associated phenotype.
Differences in initial adherence or adaptation to culture conditions could explain growth rate differences.
required_assumptions: Growth rates in vitro reflect intrinsic proliferative capacity rather than culture adaptation.
Cell cycle snapshot at 24 hr is representative of overall cell cycle dynamics.
AMIECs and HCAECs are at comparable passage numbers.
evaluation.notes: The interpretation that 'all phases are equally affected' from a null result in cell cycle distribution is logically weak — absence of evidence is not evidence of absence, especially with n=3 and likely low statistical power.

nodes.label: AMIECs display impaired migration capacity in wound-healing assays compared to c…
nodes.claim: AMIECs display impaired migration capacity in wound-healing assays compared to control HCAECs.
nodes.verbatim_quote: three AMIECs displayed wound closure rates below 50%, four others about 60%, and only one about 80% after 24 hr of migration under the same conditions

strengths: Wound healing assays were performed with mitomycin C to specifically assess migration independent of proliferation.
All 8 AMIEC lines showed reduced migration compared to the 100% closure in controls, with statistical significance reported.
Quantitative data with error bars and statistical testing are provided.
weaknesses: Only one control cell line was used as a comparator.
n=3 — unclear if biological or technical replicates.
Mitomycin C at 1 mg/mL is an extremely high concentration (typical is 5-10 μg/mL); this could differentially affect AMIECs vs. HCAECs and confound results.
No alternative migration assay (e.g., Boyden chamber/transwell) was used to validate findings.
alternative_interpretations: Differential sensitivity to mitomycin C between AMIECs and HCAECs could contribute to apparent migration differences.
Cell-substrate adhesion differences could affect migration independent of intrinsic migratory capacity.
required_assumptions: Mitomycin C treatment does not differentially affect AMIECs and HCAECs beyond growth inhibition.
Wound healing assays accurately reflect endothelial migration capacity.
evaluation.notes: The mitomycin C concentration stated (1 mg/mL) appears to be an error or an unusually high dose that warrants clarification.

nodes.label: AMIECs display significantly reduced tubulogenic potential, which is linked to d…
nodes.claim: AMIECs display significantly reduced tubulogenic potential, which is linked to defective migration rather than abnormal proliferation.
nodes.verbatim_quote: The branching capacity of the AMIECs derived from different patients was linearly correlated (R2=0.67) with their ability to migrate regardless of their growth rates suggesting that the deficient tubulogenesis or sprouting of these cells is linked to a defect in their migration properties

strengths: Quantitative scoring of branching points from triplicate experiments with statistical testing.
The correlation analysis between migration and tubulogenesis (R²=0.67) adds analytical depth and distinguishes migration defects from proliferation defects.
weaknesses: R²=0.67 with only 9 data points (8 AMIECs + 1 control) is not compelling — the control HCAEC serves as a leverage point that could artificially inflate the correlation.
The claim that tubulogenesis is 'linked to migration rather than proliferation' requires demonstrating no correlation with proliferation; this is implied but not shown.
Matrigel-based tube formation assays have known limitations in reflecting true angiogenic potential.
With only 9 data points, 'linear correlation' should be interpreted cautiously.
alternative_interpretations: Both migration and tubulogenesis could be independently affected by a common upstream cause (e.g., cytoskeletal defects) without one causing the other.
The correlation could be driven by the control data point being an outlier on both axes.
required_assumptions: A linear model is appropriate for this relationship.
The correlation is not driven by the single control data point.
Matrigel tube formation reflects meaningful angiogenic potential.
evaluation.notes: The R²=0.67 correlation with 9 points including the control as a clear outlier is not strong evidence for the stated conclusion.

nodes.label: Six out of 8 AMIECs consume glucose at significantly lower rates than control HC…
nodes.claim: Six out of 8 AMIECs consume glucose at significantly lower rates than control HCAECs, while two consume more.
nodes.verbatim_quote: 6 out of the 8 AMIECs consumed glucose at significantly lower rates than control HCAECs, which may reconcile with the lower growth rates of patient-derived cells, while two patient-derived cell lines consumed more glucose than control cells.

strengths: Direct measurement of glucose in culture media by spectrophotometry is a standard, reliable method.
The result is consistent across 6/8 lines, with statistical significance reported.
The two exceptions are transparently reported.
weaknesses: Glucose consumption from media does not distinguish between glycolytic consumption and consumption by other pathways (PPP, hexosamine biosynthesis, etc.).
No normalization to cell number or protein content for glucose consumption rate is clearly described, though the growth rate differences could confound media consumption data.
Measurements at a single 48-hr timepoint may not capture dynamics.
alternative_interpretations: Lower glucose consumption could simply reflect fewer cells (slower growth) rather than intrinsically lower glycolytic rates per cell.
required_assumptions: Glucose consumption is normalized appropriately to cell number.
Media glucose depletion reflects cellular metabolic activity rather than medium degradation or other artifacts.
evaluation.notes: The normalization method for glucose consumption is critical but not clearly stated in the methods.

nodes.label: PFKFB3 protein levels are significantly lower in 7 out of 8 AMIECs, consistent w…
nodes.claim: PFKFB3 protein levels are significantly lower in 7 out of 8 AMIECs, consistent with lower glycolytic flux.
nodes.verbatim_quote: finding significantly lower levels in 7 out of the 8 AMIECs, as compared to control HCAECs, consistent with their lower glucose uptake

strengths: Western blotting for PFKFB3 was quantified from triplicate experiments normalized to β-actin.
7/8 lines showing lower PFKFB3 is a consistent finding.
CE-45 serves as an informative internal control — near-normal PFKFB3 and higher glucose consumption.
weaknesses: β-actin normalization can be unreliable if actin expression varies between cell types.
No mRNA expression data (qRT-PCR) to distinguish transcriptional vs. post-transcriptional regulation.
No PFKFB3 activity assay or F2,6BP measurement.
alternative_interpretations: PFKFB3 downregulation could be a consequence of reduced metabolic demand in slowly growing cells rather than a primary glycolytic defect.
required_assumptions: β-actin is an appropriate loading control for these comparisons.
PFKFB3 protein level reflects PFKFB3 functional activity.

nodes.label: All AMIECs produce high levels of lactate regardless of glucose uptake, represen…
nodes.claim: All AMIECs produce high levels of lactate regardless of glucose uptake, representing an uncoupling of lactate production from glycolysis that suggests an alternative lactate source.
nodes.verbatim_quote: all AMIECs displayed a strong production of lactate, comparable or superior to control cells, regardless of their levels of glucose uptake

strengths: Lactate production data from all 8 lines consistently shows high production.
The uncoupling of lactate production from glucose consumption in 6/8 lines is a genuinely interesting observation.
weaknesses: No direct evidence is provided for the 'alternative source' of lactate — the suggestion of glutaminolysis-derived lactate remains entirely speculative without tracing experiments.
Media lactate measurements may not be normalized per cell, which is critical given growth rate differences.
No LDH-A expression or activity data is presented.
alternative_interpretations: Lactate could be produced from amino acids in the culture medium (serine, alanine) or from other carbon sources besides glutamine.
If normalization to cell number is inadequate, the apparent 'high' lactate production could be an artifact.
required_assumptions: Lactate measurements are properly normalized to cell number.
The uncoupling of lactate from glucose consumption implies an alternative metabolic source rather than technical artifact.
evaluation.notes: This observation is intriguing but the proposed explanation (glutamine-derived lactate) is highly speculative without tracing data.

nodes.label: PFKFB4 is expressed at significantly higher levels in AMIECs, which together wit…
nodes.claim: PFKFB4 is expressed at significantly higher levels in AMIECs, which together with low PFKFB3 predicts redirection of glucose-6-phosphate toward the pentose phosphate pathway.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Low levels of PFKFB3 expression coupled with high levels of PFKFB4 expression in AMI patient-derived cells predict a redirection of glucose-6-phosphate (G6P) towards the PPP.

strengths: PFKFB4 upregulation is demonstrated by quantified Western blotting from triplicate experiments.
The reciprocal regulation of PFKFB3 (down) and PFKFB4 (up) is an interesting and internally consistent finding.
weaknesses: The prediction that high PFKFB4/low PFKFB3 redirects G6P toward PPP is based on literature from cancer cells and has not been validated in this endothelial cell system.
No direct measurement of G6P levels or PPP flux was performed.
PFKFB4 has been shown to have context-dependent functions — its role as a phosphatase vs. kinase varies by cell type.
The mechanistic link between PFKFB4 and PPP shunting (via SRC-3/TKT) is cited from cancer biology and may not apply here.
alternative_interpretations: High PFKFB4 could reflect a stress response or survival mechanism unrelated to PPP shunting.
PFKFB4 upregulation could serve other functions (e.g., kinase-independent roles) not considered by the authors.
required_assumptions: PFKFB4 functions primarily as a bisphosphatase in AMIECs, reducing F2,6BP and glycolytic flux.
Cancer cell biology regarding PFKFB4 function applies to coronary endothelial cells.
The PFKFB3/PFKFB4 ratio determines metabolic partitioning between glycolysis and PPP.
evaluation.notes: The prediction is biochemically reasonable but untested in this system.

nodes.label: The low PFKFB3 expression may help explain the low proliferation rates, migratio…
nodes.claim: The low PFKFB3 expression may help explain the low proliferation rates, migration capacity, and tubulogenic activity of AMIECs, as these processes require robust glycolysis.
nodes.verbatim_quote: This may also help explain, at least in part, the low proliferation rates, migration capacity, and tubulogenic activity of these cells, as these processes require robust glycolysis.

strengths: The association between PFKFB3 levels and endothelial proliferation/migration is supported by prior literature (Schoors et al., 2014; Li et al., 2019 as cited in the paper).
The internal correlation between low PFKFB3 and impaired function across patient lines provides some support.
weaknesses: No rescue experiment (e.g., PFKFB3 overexpression or pharmacological PFKFB3 activation) was performed to test causality.
Correlation between PFKFB3 levels and functional impairment across the 8 lines is not formally shown.
CE-45 has near-normal PFKFB3 but still shows functional impairment, which partially undermines this claim.
alternative_interpretations: Low PFKFB3 could be a consequence rather than a cause of the functional impairments.
Multiple other metabolic and non-metabolic factors could contribute to the functional defects independently of PFKFB3.
required_assumptions: PFKFB3-driven glycolysis is the primary metabolic driver of endothelial proliferation, migration, and tubulogenesis in this system.
Literature from other endothelial cell models applies to these patient-derived coronary ECs.
evaluation.notes: The claim uses 'may help explain' appropriately hedged language, but the lack of any causal evidence limits its support.

nodes.label: Glutamine consumption in AMIECs is higher than in control HCAECs, and the glutam…
nodes.claim: Glutamine consumption in AMIECs is higher than in control HCAECs, and the glutamine-to-glucose consumption ratio is far greater in patient-derived cells, suggesting AMIECs mainly resort to glutamine as their carbon source.
nodes.verbatim_quote: This suggests that AMI patient-derived cells mainly resort to glutamine, rather than glucose, as their carbon source.

strengths: Glutamine consumption was directly measured and is higher in AMIECs.
The glutamine-to-glucose ratio provides a useful integrative metric.
weaknesses: The leap from 'higher glutamine-to-glucose ratio' to 'mainly resort to glutamine as their carbon source' is unjustified without carbon tracing data.
Higher glutamine consumption could serve primarily biosynthetic rather than bioenergetic needs.
Normalization to cell number is not clearly described.
The claim uses 'suggests' but the conclusion 'mainly resort to glutamine as their carbon source' is stated as if established.
alternative_interpretations: Higher glutamine consumption could primarily feed glutathione synthesis and amino acid pools rather than serving as the main carbon/energy source.
Glutamine could be consumed for nucleotide biosynthesis in cells attempting to maintain proliferation.
required_assumptions: Glutamine consumption rate reflects its use as a carbon source for energy metabolism.
The glutamine-to-glucose ratio is a meaningful indicator of carbon source preference.
evaluation.notes: This claim overstates the evidence. Without tracing data, one cannot conclude that glutamine is the 'main carbon source.'

nodes.label: Both GLS1 isoforms (KGA and GAC) are expressed at significantly higher levels in…
nodes.claim: Both GLS1 isoforms (KGA and GAC) are expressed at significantly higher levels in AMIECs than control cells, consistent with enhanced glutaminolysis.
nodes.verbatim_quote: both isoforms of GLS1, KGA, and GAC, are expressed at significantly higher levels in patient-derived cells than control cells

strengths: Isoform-specific antibodies were used to distinguish KGA and GAC.
Quantification from triplicate experiments with normalization to β-actin.
Both isoforms are consistently upregulated across patient-derived lines.
weaknesses: No glutaminase activity assay was performed — protein expression does not necessarily reflect enzymatic activity.
No mRNA data to distinguish transcriptional vs. post-transcriptional regulation.
GLS2 expression was not examined.
alternative_interpretations: GLS1 upregulation could be a response to culture conditions or acidic environment from lactate accumulation rather than a disease-specific feature.
required_assumptions: GLS1 protein expression correlates with glutaminase activity.
β-actin is a reliable loading control.

nodes.label: Lower extracellular glutamate export despite high glutaminase levels suggests ro…
nodes.claim: Lower extracellular glutamate export despite high glutaminase levels suggests robust intracellular consumption of glutamate for glutathione production in AMIECs.
nodes.verbatim_quote: the lower levels of extracellular export of glutamate are suggestive of a robust consumption of glutamate in the production of GSH in these cells.

strengths: The logic is internally consistent: high glutaminase + low extracellular glutamate export = intracellular glutamate consumption.
Intracellular glutamate levels were confirmed as elevated by GC/MS.
weaknesses: The conclusion that glutamate is consumed specifically for GSH production is one of several possible fates and is not directly demonstrated.
No measurement of GSH synthesis rate or γ-glutamylcysteine synthetase expression/activity was performed.
Glutamate could be consumed for protein synthesis, transamination reactions, or other metabolic pathways.
2/8 lines show glutamate production comparable to controls, weakening the generality.
alternative_interpretations: Intracellular glutamate accumulation with low export could reflect a transporter defect rather than increased consumption.
Glutamate could be preferentially channeled into α-KG for TCA cycle anaplerosis rather than GSH synthesis.
required_assumptions: Low extracellular glutamate export combined with high intracellular glutamate implies high intracellular consumption.
The primary fate of intracellular glutamate in AMIECs is GSH synthesis.
evaluation.notes: The inference chain is plausible but involves several unverified assumptions about glutamate fate.

nodes.label: High lactate production in AMIECs with low glucose consumption could be explaine…
nodes.claim: High lactate production in AMIECs with low glucose consumption could be explained by glutamine-derived pyruvate conversion to lactate, consistent with the strong glutamine consumption observed.
nodes.verbatim_quote: under conditions of low glucose consumption and evidence of low glycolytic activity, an alternative source is needed that may explain high lactate production from pyruvate in AMIECs. One possibility is through glutamine-initiated metabolism

strengths: The hypothesis is biochemically plausible and referenced to prior work in pancreatic cancer cells.
The observation of high lactate with low glucose is indeed a conundrum that requires explanation.
weaknesses: No 13C-glutamine tracing was performed to demonstrate glutamine-derived lactate production.
No measurement of malic enzyme expression or activity was performed.
No measurement of LDH-A expression or activity.
The evidence comes entirely from pancreatic cancer cells and has never been demonstrated in endothelial cells.
This is explicitly framed as 'one possibility' in the text — it is a hypothesis, not a supported claim.
alternative_interpretations: Lactate could derive from other amino acids or from serum components in the culture medium.
Measurement artifacts or normalization issues could account for the apparent uncoupling.
Low glucose uptake could feed glycolysis more efficiently than assumed, producing sufficient pyruvate for lactate production.
required_assumptions: The malic enzyme pathway is sufficiently active in endothelial cells to produce significant amounts of lactate.
Glutamine-derived pyruvate contributes meaningfully to total lactate production.
Findings in pancreatic cancer cells translate to coronary endothelial cells.
evaluation.notes: This is purely speculative. The authors appropriately hedge but this claim should not be represented as supported.

nodes.label: MitoProbe DiIC1(5) accumulated at significantly higher levels in all AMIECs rela…
nodes.claim: MitoProbe DiIC1(5) accumulated at significantly higher levels in all AMIECs relative to control HCAECs, indicating mitochondrial hyperpolarization.
nodes.verbatim_quote: MitoProbe accumulated at significantly higher levels in all AMIECs relative to control HCAECs, indicating a mitochondrial hyperpolarization due to increased membrane potentials.

strengths: DiIC1(5) data is consistent across all 8 AMIEC lines — this is the most universal finding in the paper.
CCCP control confirms the signal is mitochondrial-membrane-potential-dependent.
Statistical significance is reported.
weaknesses: DiIC1(5) is sensitive to mitochondrial mass; differences in mitochondrial content between AMIECs and HCAECs could confound results. No mitochondrial mass normalization was performed.
A single dye was used — dual-dye approaches (e.g., JC-1 or TMRM with MitoTracker Green normalization) would be more rigorous.
No quantification of the CCCP depolarization data is shown — it is described qualitatively.
alternative_interpretations: Higher DiIC1(5) signal could reflect greater mitochondrial mass rather than higher membrane potential per mitochondrion.
required_assumptions: DiIC1(5) accumulation faithfully reflects membrane potential rather than mitochondrial mass.
AMIECs and HCAECs have comparable mitochondrial mass.
evaluation.notes: The universality of the finding across all 8 lines is notable and the CCCP control is important, but the absence of mitochondrial mass normalization is a real concern.

nodes.label: The increased ROS levels in AMIECs cannot be attributed to environmental factors…
nodes.claim: The increased ROS levels in AMIECs cannot be attributed to environmental factors since the cells are in identical in vitro conditions to controls, and thus likely originate from endogenous signals impinging on mitochondria or NAD(P)H oxidases.
nodes.verbatim_quote: our patient-derived cells are no longer in an in vivo environment and are rather in an in vitro environment identical to that of control endothelial cells, and, therefore, their increased ROS levels cannot be directly attributed to environmental factors.

strengths: The logic that in vitro conditions are identical for AMIECs and HCAECs is correct, ruling out current environmental differences as a cause of differential ROS.
The authors acknowledge multiple potential endogenous ROS sources (mitochondria, NAD(P)H oxidases).
weaknesses: The argument that identical in vitro conditions rule out environmental factors is incomplete — the cells come from fundamentally different in vivo environments and their in vitro state may carry the effects of prior exposure.
The authors themselves acknowledge epigenetic imprints as a possibility, which could include environmentally-induced changes that persist in culture.
No NOX enzyme expression or activity was measured to distinguish mitochondrial from cytoplasmic ROS sources.
MitoSOX was not used to specifically measure mitochondrial ROS.
alternative_interpretations: Epigenetic memory of in vivo oxidative stress could maintain elevated ROS production programs.
Accumulated genetic mutations in cells from atherosclerotic lesions could drive higher ROS.
Higher ROS could reflect defective antioxidant capacity despite elevated glutathione (e.g., other antioxidant systems could be impaired).
required_assumptions: Identical culture conditions eliminate environmental contributions to differential ROS levels.
Cells have 'reset' from their in vivo environmental exposures after sufficient passages.
evaluation.notes: The reasoning here is somewhat circular — the authors argue that the cells are in identical conditions, therefore differences must be cell-autonomous, but they also suggest epigenetic imprints which are by definition environmental in origin.

nodes.label: AMIECs operate contrary to normal endothelial cells, which rely mostly on glycol…
nodes.claim: AMIECs operate contrary to normal endothelial cells, which rely mostly on glycolysis rather than mitochondrial respiration for energy production.
nodes.verbatim_quote: contrary to physiologically normal ECs, which rely mostly on glycolysis for energy production rather than mitochondrial respiration, AMIECs display low levels of glycolysis...while also displaying a high membrane potential, suggestive of a high mitochondrial activity.

strengths: The observation that AMIECs have low glycolysis metrics and high membrane potential is consistent with a shift away from glycolysis-dominant metabolism.
weaknesses: No direct measurement of mitochondrial respiration (oxygen consumption rate) was performed. 'High membrane potential suggestive of high mitochondrial activity' is indirect evidence at best.
High membrane potential does not necessarily mean high respiration — it could mean impaired ATP synthase or reduced ATP consumption.
The comparison to 'normal ECs which rely mostly on glycolysis' is based on literature rather than demonstrated in the specific HCAEC control used in this study.
alternative_interpretations: High membrane potential could indicate mitochondrial dysfunction (e.g., impaired complex V) rather than increased respiratory activity.
AMIECs may still rely on glycolysis but process glucose less efficiently.
required_assumptions: High mitochondrial membrane potential equals high mitochondrial respiratory activity.
Low glycolytic markers necessarily mean a shift to mitochondrial respiration rather than reduced overall metabolism.
evaluation.notes: The absence of Seahorse or Clark electrode oxygen consumption measurements is the most significant experimental gap in the paper for supporting claims about mitochondrial activity.

nodes.label: G6PD expression and enzyme activity are significantly higher in AMIECs than cont…
nodes.claim: G6PD expression and enzyme activity are significantly higher in AMIECs than controls, supporting enhanced activity of the oxidative branch of the PPP.
nodes.verbatim_quote: we found significantly higher levels of G6PD in AMIECs than in control cells...Likewise, AMIECs displayed higher levels of G6PD enzyme activity than control cells.

strengths: Both protein expression (Western blotting, triplicate, quantified) and enzyme activity were measured for G6PD.
Concordance between expression and activity provides strong evidence.
CE-45 again serves as an informative internal exception with near-normal levels.
weaknesses: G6PD is the rate-limiting enzyme of the oxidative PPP, but no downstream PPP metabolites (6-phosphogluconate, ribose-5-phosphate, NADPH) were measured.
G6PD can be regulated allosterically — higher expression and higher in vitro activity don't guarantee higher in vivo PPP flux.
alternative_interpretations: G6PD upregulation could be a direct stress response to ROS rather than evidence of a metabolic shunt from glycolysis.
required_assumptions: G6PD expression and activity correlate with actual PPP flux in intact cells.
evaluation.notes: This is one of the stronger pieces of evidence in the paper because both expression and activity were measured.

nodes.label: Seven of 8 AMIECs contain ROS at significantly higher levels than control cells,…
nodes.claim: Seven of 8 AMIECs contain ROS at significantly higher levels than control cells, and all 8 have increased intracellular reduced glutathione, suggesting glutathione is upregulated to counter excess ROS.
nodes.verbatim_quote: These observations suggest that glutathione levels are upregulated in AMIECs to counter excess ROS levels.

strengths: ROS and glutathione measurements are consistent across 7/8 and 8/8 lines respectively.
The anti-correlation (high ROS + high GSH) is biologically coherent as a compensatory response.
CE-45 as a consistent outlier strengthens the overall pattern.
weaknesses: H2DCFDA measures total cellular ROS, not specifically mitochondrial ROS — cannot determine source.
No oxidative damage markers (e.g., 8-OHdG, lipid peroxidation) were measured to assess whether the elevated ROS causes actual damage or is fully compensated by glutathione.
Correlation between ROS and GSH is consistent with compensatory upregulation but does not prove causality.
alternative_interpretations: High GSH could be a cause of altered metabolism (by affecting signaling pathways) rather than merely a compensatory response to ROS.
Elevated ROS could have functional signaling roles rather than being purely pathological.
required_assumptions: H2DCFDA reliably quantifies ROS levels across different cell types.
GSH upregulation is a response to ROS rather than an independent metabolic feature.
evaluation.notes: The consistency across cell lines is compelling.

nodes.label: Elevated intracellular cysteine and glutamate levels in AMIECs are consistent wi…
nodes.claim: Elevated intracellular cysteine and glutamate levels in AMIECs are consistent with higher glutathione biosynthesis.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Cysteine and glutamate play important roles in the synthesis of glutathione (GSH) and both had significantly higher concentrations in all AMIECs, consistent with higher levels of GSH as compared to control cells.

strengths: GC/MS is a reliable analytical method for intracellular amino acid quantification.
Both cysteine and glutamate — the two critical GSH precursors — are elevated, which is consistent with enhanced GSH biosynthesis.
Data is consistent across all AMIECs.
weaknesses: Elevated cysteine and glutamate are consistent with but do not prove increased GSH biosynthetic flux — they could also reflect increased import or decreased utilization in other pathways.
No measurement of γ-glutamylcysteine synthetase or glutathione synthetase expression/activity.
Glycine, the third GSH component, is not elevated — this is noted but not discussed.
alternative_interpretations: Elevated cysteine and glutamate could reflect altered amino acid transport or protein catabolism rather than specifically enhanced GSH biosynthesis.
The fact that glycine is not elevated could suggest GSH synthesis is not uniformly upregulated at the substrate level.
required_assumptions: Elevated intracellular cysteine and glutamate indicate enhanced GSH biosynthesis rather than other metabolic fates.
evaluation.notes: The absence of elevated glycine (the third GSH amino acid) deserves discussion.

nodes.label: Aspartate was found at increased levels in AMIECs, consistent with higher mitoch…
nodes.claim: Aspartate was found at increased levels in AMIECs, consistent with higher mitochondrial respiration and anaplerotic use of glutamate, and contributes to offset high ROS through NAD+ and NADPH production.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Aspartate derived from oxaloacetate, via glutaminolysis, produces NAD+, required for glycolysis and NADPH, needed for redox balance.

strengths: Aspartate levels were measured by GC/MS and found to be elevated in AMIECs.
The connection between aspartate and NAD+/NADPH production through the malate-aspartate shuttle is biochemically sound.
weaknesses: The claim that elevated aspartate specifically reflects 'higher mitochondrial respiration and anaplerotic use of glutamate' is not directly demonstrated — many pathways produce aspartate.
No flux analysis was performed to determine whether aspartate is being synthesized from oxaloacetate via glutaminolysis.
The sentence about aspartate producing NAD+ and NADPH is duplicated in the text, suggesting possible editing errors.
Aspartate is also an essential precursor for nucleotide synthesis and protein synthesis.
alternative_interpretations: Elevated aspartate could reflect reduced utilization (lower nucleotide synthesis in slowly growing cells) rather than increased production.
Aspartate accumulation could indicate impaired purine/pyrimidine synthesis pathways.
required_assumptions: Elevated aspartate indicates increased mitochondrial glutamate oxidation.
Aspartate is primarily derived from the TCA cycle via glutaminolysis in these cells.
evaluation.notes: The duplicated sentence about aspartate/NAD+/NADPH in the text suggests hasty manuscript preparation.

nodes.label: The two primary cell-autonomous deficiencies are: (1) strong mitochondrial proto…
nodes.claim: The two primary cell-autonomous deficiencies are: (1) strong mitochondrial proton coupling causing excess ROS countered by enhanced NADPH and glutathione, and (2) a glucose-to-glutamine carbon source switch as an adaptive mechanism for glutathione production and NAD+ replenishment.
nodes.verbatim_quote: our observations and evidence by others suggest the occurrence of two cell-autonomous, primary deficiencies in AMI patient-derived ECs

strengths: The summary integrates multiple observations into a coherent model.
The two deficiencies are conceptually distinct and map onto different experimental observations.
weaknesses: Designating these as 'primary deficiencies' implies they are causes rather than consequences — this causality has not been established.
No perturbation experiments were performed to test whether these are truly primary (upstream) deficiencies or secondary adaptations.
It is unclear whether these represent two independent deficiencies or a single root cause with two manifestations.
The word 'primary' is scientifically unjustified by the correlative data presented.
alternative_interpretations: Both 'deficiencies' could be downstream consequences of a single upstream cause (e.g., epigenetic reprogramming, somatic mutations).
The metabolic phenotype could be an adaptive response that is actually protective rather than a deficiency.
required_assumptions: The mitochondrial hyperpolarization is a primary defect rather than a secondary consequence.
The carbon source switch is an independent primary deficiency rather than a compensatory response.
These are deficiencies (pathological) rather than adaptations (potentially protective).
evaluation.notes: The distinction between primary deficiency and secondary adaptation cannot be made from correlative data alone.

nodes.label: Pharmacological uncouplers could revert the observed mitochondrial dysfunction a…
nodes.claim: Pharmacological uncouplers could revert the observed mitochondrial dysfunction and mitigate ROS production and the accompanying metabolic reprogramming.
nodes.verbatim_quote: a possible intervention to revert the observed mitochondrial dysfunction would be the use of pharmacological uncouplers to mitigate ROS production and the accompanying metabolic reprogramming

strengths: The hypothesis is grounded in published literature on mitochondrial uncoupling and ROS.
The Gu et al. (2021) reference provides in vivo precedent for the concept.
weaknesses: No uncoupling experiment was performed in AMIECs — this is entirely speculative.
No rescue experiment of any kind was performed in this study.
The referenced Gu et al. study is in animal models, not human endothelial cells.
Pharmacological uncouplers could have deleterious effects on ATP production and cell viability that are not considered.
The claim that uncoupling would 'revert' the entire metabolic reprogramming is a large extrapolation.
alternative_interpretations: Uncoupling could reduce membrane potential without affecting the metabolic reprogramming if the latter is driven by other mechanisms (e.g., epigenetic).
Uncoupling might be harmful to already dysfunctional cells by further compromising energy production.
required_assumptions: Mitochondrial hyperpolarization is the primary driver of the metabolic phenotype.
ROS reduction via uncoupling would be sufficient to reverse all downstream metabolic changes.
Animal model results with UCP1 are translatable to human AMI endothelial cells.
evaluation.notes: This is the most important claim for clinical relevance but has zero experimental support in this paper.

nodes.label: The metabolic dysfunction could originate from primary mitochondrial defects (in…
nodes.claim: The metabolic dysfunction could originate from primary mitochondrial defects (inherited or acquired) or from epigenetic imprints of in vivo exposure persisting ex vivo.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Primary dysfunctions in mitochondria, from either inherited or acquired genetic defects, have been suggested as underlying causes of atherogenic pathologies...Alternatively, our AIMECs might continue to carry, ex-vivo, epigenetic imprints of their exposure to factors and cells while in the patients

strengths: Both possibilities (genetic defects, epigenetic imprints) are plausible and appropriately presented as hypotheses.
The acknowledgment of uncertainty about the origin is scientifically honest.
weaknesses: No genetic analysis (whole exome, targeted sequencing, or mitochondrial DNA sequencing) was performed.
No epigenetic analysis (methylation profiling, histone modification analysis) was performed.
No passage-dependent analysis was done to test whether the phenotype is stable across many passages (which would support epigenetic or genetic origin) or fades (suggesting culture adaptation).
These remain pure speculations without any supporting data.
alternative_interpretations: The phenotype could simply reflect selection of a subpopulation during the isolation and culture process.
The cells could carry somatic mutations from the atherosclerotic plaque environment (e.g., clonal hematopoiesis-like mutations).
required_assumptions: The metabolic phenotype has a persistent genetic or epigenetic basis.
The in vitro phenotype reflects in vivo cellular states.
evaluation.notes: Both proposed origins are mentioned as possibilities but neither is investigated experimentally.

nodes.label: Blunted p53 function could be a driver of PFKFB4 upregulation in AMIECs, as PFKF…
nodes.claim: Blunted p53 function could be a driver of PFKFB4 upregulation in AMIECs, as PFKFB4 is strongly upregulated in the absence of p53.
nodes.verbatim_quote: The hypothesis of a blunted function of p53 as a driver of PFKFB4 upregulation in these cells could merit further investigation.

strengths: The hypothesis is grounded in published literature (Ros et al., 2017 as cited) showing PFKFB4 upregulation in the absence of p53.
The pattern (PFKFB3 down, PFKFB4 up) is consistent with blunted p53 function.
weaknesses: No p53 status was determined in AMIECs (expression, mutation, activity).
No p53 target gene expression analysis was performed.
The hypothesis is explicitly acknowledged as speculative ('could merit further investigation').
PFKFB4 upregulation could occur through many mechanisms independent of p53.
alternative_interpretations: PFKFB4 upregulation could be driven by HIF-1α (even in normoxia through pseudo-hypoxic signaling), mTOR, or other pathways.
PFKFB4 could be upregulated through post-transcriptional mechanisms independent of transcriptional regulation.
required_assumptions: p53 function is blunted in AMIECs.
p53 regulation of PFKFB4 in cancer cells applies to endothelial cells.
PFKFB4 transcriptional regulation is the dominant mechanism of its upregulation.
evaluation.notes: This is appropriately labeled as hypothesis but presented alongside supported claims without clear distinction.

nodes.label: Western blotting confirmed expression of V-CAM1, PECAM-1, CD-34, and CD-105 endo…
nodes.claim: Western blotting confirmed expression of V-CAM1, PECAM-1, CD-34, and CD-105 endothelial markers in AMIECs.
nodes.verbatim_quote: The endothelial nature of these cells was confirmed by Western blotting for the expression of the endothelial markers, V-CAM1 (vascular cell adhesion protein 1, CD-106), PECAM-1 (platelet endothelial cell adhesion molecule, CD31), CD-34, and CD-105 (endoglin)

strengths: Four distinct endothelial markers were used.
Source data for Western blots are referenced (Figure 1—source data 1 and 2).
weaknesses: No quantification of marker expression levels is provided.
No flow cytometric confirmation was performed.
The figure legend mentions CD-10 rather than CD-105, raising concerns about accuracy.
required_assumptions: Western blotting of these four markers is sufficient for endothelial identification.

nodes.label: AMIECs at 80% confluence presented expected shape and appeared similar to contro…
nodes.claim: AMIECs at 80% confluence presented expected shape and appeared similar to control HCAECs under bright field imaging.
nodes.verbatim_quote: At 80% confluence, AMIECs presented the expected shape and appeared similar to control HCAECs

strengths: Bright field images at 10x and 20x are provided for both AMIECs and HCAECs.
Morphological similarity is a basic but important checkpoint.
weaknesses: Morphological assessment is subjective and qualitative.
Representative images may not capture the full heterogeneity of AMIECs.
required_assumptions: Morphological similarity under bright field imaging reflects endothelial identity.

nodes.label: After 168 hr, control HCAECs reached a growth plateau while AMIECs continued to …
nodes.claim: After 168 hr, control HCAECs reached a growth plateau while AMIECs continued to proliferate exponentially at slow rates without reaching saturation.
nodes.verbatim_quote: after 168 hr, while control HCAECs had reached a plateau in their growth, AMIECs continued to proliferate exponentially, albeit at slow rates, without reaching saturation.

strengths: Growth was monitored over an extended period (168 hr) with error bars and n=3.
The qualitative difference (plateau vs. continued exponential growth) is clearly described.
weaknesses: It is unclear whether n=3 represents biological or technical replicates.
Only one control line means normal variation in growth kinetics is unknown.
Starting cell density and passage number are not reported.
alternative_interpretations: Control HCAECs may reach plateau due to contact inhibition at different cell densities than AMIECs, which grow more slowly.
required_assumptions: Growth conditions were identical and starting conditions equivalent.
Passage-matched comparisons were made.

nodes.label: Flow cytometry at 24 hr showed no significant differences in cell cycle phase di…
nodes.claim: Flow cytometry at 24 hr showed no significant differences in cell cycle phase distribution between AMIECs and controls, with only a modest non-significant tendency to accumulate in G1.
nodes.verbatim_quote: we observed no significant differences in the distribution of cell cycle phases between AMIECs and control cells, except for a modest tendency, without reaching statistical significance, of AMIECs to accumulate in the G1 phase

strengths: Flow cytometry is an appropriate method for cell cycle analysis.
The null result (no significant differences) is honestly reported.
weaknesses: Only a single time point (24 hr) was assessed.
n=3 may be underpowered to detect modest cell cycle shifts.
No BrdU or EdU incorporation assays were performed for S-phase quantification.
The time point chosen (24 hr = 'maximum growth in controls') may not be representative for AMIECs with different growth kinetics.
alternative_interpretations: The modest G1 trend could be real but the study is underpowered to detect it.
Cell cycle distribution at 24 hr may not reflect the steady-state dynamics.
required_assumptions: A single time point flow cytometry measurement captures relevant cell cycle dynamics.
n=3 is sufficient for this comparison.

nodes.label: Control HCAECs achieved complete wound closure after 24 hr, while AMIECs showed …
nodes.claim: Control HCAECs achieved complete wound closure after 24 hr, while AMIECs showed 50-80% closure rates under the same conditions (p≤0.05 to p≤0.001).
nodes.verbatim_quote: control HCAECs achieved a complete closure of the wound after 24 hr of seeding. In contrast, three AMIECs displayed wound closure rates below 50%, four others about 60%, and only one about 80%

strengths: Quantitative wound closure percentages are provided for each cell line.
Statistical significance is reported with appropriate tests.
Mitomycin C was used to control for proliferation.
weaknesses: The concentration of mitomycin C (1 mg/mL) is extremely high and potentially confounding.
n=3, unclear biological vs. technical replicates.
required_assumptions: Mitomycin C at the stated concentration does not differentially affect cell viability between AMIECs and HCAECs.
evaluation.notes: The 1 mg/mL mitomycin C concentration should be verified — standard concentrations are typically 1-10 μg/mL.

nodes.label: Control HCAECs averaged 80 branching points while AMIECs showed significantly fe…
nodes.claim: Control HCAECs averaged 80 branching points while AMIECs showed significantly fewer branching points and shorter, fragmented tubes after 12 hr of VEGF stimulation.
nodes.verbatim_quote: While control HCAECs averaged 80 branching points, AMIECs displayed a significantly reduced tubulogenic potential, evident both as a diminished number of branching points and as shorter and fragmented tubes

strengths: Quantification of branch points from triplicate experiments with statistical testing.
Both quantitative (branch points) and qualitative (tube length, fragmentation) assessments are described.
Representative images and ImageJ-based quantification add rigor.
weaknesses: Growth factor-free Matrigel may introduce variability.
Only 5 random fields per condition were scored.
Matrigel tube assay limitations are well-known in the field.
required_assumptions: Matrigel tube formation assay reflects angiogenic potential.

nodes.label: Branching capacity correlated linearly with migration ability (R²=0.67) regardle…
nodes.claim: Branching capacity correlated linearly with migration ability (R²=0.67) regardless of growth rates.
nodes.verbatim_quote: The branching capacity of the AMIECs derived from different patients was linearly correlated (R2=0.67) with their ability to migrate regardless of their growth rates

strengths: The correlation analysis adds an integrative dimension to the individual assay results.
weaknesses: R²=0.67 with only 9 data points (including the control as a clear outlier on both axes) is statistically weak.
No regression diagnostics (p-value, confidence interval) are reported for the correlation.
The control data point likely acts as a leverage point driving the apparent correlation.
The claim 'regardless of growth rates' is asserted but no correlation between growth and tubulogenesis is shown to demonstrate its absence.
alternative_interpretations: Remove the control data point and the correlation may substantially weaken or disappear.
Both migration and tubulogenesis could be independently correlated with a third variable.
required_assumptions: The correlation is not driven by the control leverage point.
Nine data points are sufficient for meaningful linear regression.
evaluation.notes: Critical to test this correlation without the control point and to show that growth does not correlate with either outcome.

nodes.label: Spectrophotometric measurement of glucose in culture media after 48 hr showed 6/…
nodes.claim: Spectrophotometric measurement of glucose in culture media after 48 hr showed 6/8 AMIECs with significantly lower glucose consumption (p≤0.05 to p≤0.001) and 2 with higher consumption than HCAECs.
nodes.verbatim_quote: 6 out of the 8 AMIECs consumed glucose at significantly lower rates than control HCAECs...while two patient-derived cell lines consumed more glucose than control cells.

strengths: Spectrophotometric measurement is a standard, validated method for glucose quantification.
Statistical significance is reported for each comparison.
weaknesses: Normalization method (per cell, per protein, per well) is not clearly stated.
A single 48-hr timepoint may not capture consumption dynamics.
required_assumptions: Measurements are appropriately normalized to cell number or biomass.

nodes.label: CE-45, one of two high glucose consumers, expressed PFKFB3 at levels close to co…
nodes.claim: CE-45, one of two high glucose consumers, expressed PFKFB3 at levels close to control cells, reinforcing the association between low PFKFB3 and low glucose uptake.
nodes.verbatim_quote: one of the two patient-derived cell lines with high glucose uptake, CE-45, expressed PFKFB3 at levels close to those of control cells, thus reinforcing the notion that cell lines with low glucose uptake have low rates of glycolysis.

strengths: CE-45 serves as an informative internal reference, strengthening the PFKFB3-glucose consumption association.
The observation is internally consistent with other data in the paper.
weaknesses: This is a single data point (one cell line); the association could be coincidental.
CE-61 also has high glucose consumption but its PFKFB3 level is not specifically discussed as a counterexample.
alternative_interpretations: CE-45 could simply be the least diseased cell line rather than confirming a specific PFKFB3-glucose link.
required_assumptions: CE-45's near-normal PFKFB3 is causally related to its glucose consumption rather than coincidental.
evaluation.notes: CE-61 should also be discussed — it has high glucose consumption but its PFKFB3 status is not clarified.

nodes.label: Spectrophotometric determination of lactate in culture media showed all AMIECs w…
nodes.claim: Spectrophotometric determination of lactate in culture media showed all AMIECs with strong lactate production comparable or superior to controls, independent of glucose consumption levels.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Remarkably, all AMIECs displayed a strong production of lactate, comparable or superior to control cells, regardless of their levels of glucose uptake

strengths: Lactate measurements are consistent across all 8 lines.
The dissociation between glucose and lactate in 6/8 lines is clearly demonstrated.
weaknesses: Normalization to cell number is not clearly described.
No glucose-to-lactate conversion ratio was calculated for direct comparison.
required_assumptions: Lactate measurements are properly normalized.
evaluation.notes: The figure legend mentions 'Conversion rate of glucose to lactate' (Figure 3B) but this appears to be a separate panel from lactate production.

nodes.label: Western blotting showed significantly higher PFKFB4 protein levels in AMIECs com…
nodes.claim: Western blotting showed significantly higher PFKFB4 protein levels in AMIECs compared to control cells (triplicate experiments, normalized to β-actin).
nodes.verbatim_quote: We also determined PFKFB4 protein levels, finding significantly higher levels of expression in AMIECs compared to control cells

strengths: Triplicate experiments with β-actin normalization.
Source data referenced.
Consistent finding across most AMIEC lines.
weaknesses: Same β-actin normalization concerns as PFKFB3.
No activity assay for PFKFB4.
required_assumptions: β-actin is a reliable loading control.

nodes.label: Spectrophotometric measurements showed higher glutamine consumption in AMIECs an…
nodes.claim: Spectrophotometric measurements showed higher glutamine consumption in AMIECs and a far greater glutamine-to-glucose consumption ratio compared to control HCAECs.
nodes.verbatim_quote: the glutamine-to-glucose consumption ratio is far greater in patient-derived cells than in control cells

strengths: Direct measurement of glutamine in media by spectrophotometry.
The glutamine-to-glucose ratio is a useful derived metric.
weaknesses: Normalization method unclear.
The figure legend appears somewhat inconsistent (Figure 5A mentions 'Glutamine and glucose production levels' — glucose consumption should be negative).
required_assumptions: Glutamine consumption from media reflects cellular glutamine utilization.

nodes.label: Western blotting with isoform-specific antibodies showed significantly higher KG…
nodes.claim: Western blotting with isoform-specific antibodies showed significantly higher KGA and GAC protein levels in AMIECs, with a higher KGA/GAC ratio.
nodes.verbatim_quote: both isoforms of GLS1, KGA, and GAC, are expressed at significantly higher levels in patient-derived cells than control cells, with a higher KGA/GAC ratio in AMIECs

strengths: Isoform-specific antibodies distinguish KGA from GAC.
Quantification from triplicate experiments.
KGA/GAC ratio provides additional characterization.
weaknesses: No enzymatic activity assay for glutaminase.
Source data referenced for verification.
required_assumptions: Isoform-specific antibodies are reliable.
Protein levels reflect enzyme activity.

nodes.label: Extracellular glutamate levels were lower in 6/8 AMIECs and the glutamate produc…
nodes.claim: Extracellular glutamate levels were lower in 6/8 AMIECs and the glutamate production-to-glutamine consumption ratio was considerably lower in AMIECs compared to controls.
nodes.verbatim_quote: the ratio between glutamate production and glutamine consumption was considerably lower in AMIECs

strengths: Both extracellular glutamate levels and the glutamate/glutamine ratio are reported.
The finding is consistent across most (6/8) AMIEC lines.
weaknesses: 2/8 lines do not show the expected pattern.
The glutamate export measurement does not directly measure intracellular glutamate fate.
alternative_interpretations: Lower glutamate export could reflect altered transporter expression rather than increased intracellular consumption.
required_assumptions: Extracellular glutamate reflects the balance of intracellular production and consumption.

nodes.label: Flow cytometry with DiIC1(5) showed significantly higher fluorescence in all AMI…
nodes.claim: Flow cytometry with DiIC1(5) showed significantly higher fluorescence in all AMIECs compared to HCAECs, with CCCP addition causing rapid depolarization confirming proton gradient dissipation.
nodes.verbatim_quote: MitoProbe accumulated at significantly higher levels in all AMIECs relative to control HCAECs...The subsequent addition of the uncoupling agent carbonyl cyanide m-chlorophenylhydrazone (CCCP) resulted in rapid depolarization

strengths: Flow cytometry provides quantitative, cell-by-cell measurements.
CCCP control is the appropriate positive control for confirming membrane potential dependence.
Consistent across all 8 AMIEC lines.
weaknesses: No mitochondrial mass control (e.g., MitoTracker Green).
Single-dye approach is less rigorous than ratiometric methods.
Statistical details of the CCCP experiment are not provided.
alternative_interpretations: Differences could partly reflect mitochondrial mass differences.
required_assumptions: DiIC1(5) accumulation reflects membrane potential independent of mitochondrial mass.

nodes.label: Western blotting showed significantly higher G6PD protein levels in AMIECs, and …
nodes.claim: Western blotting showed significantly higher G6PD protein levels in AMIECs, and enzyme activity assays confirmed higher G6PD activity (n=3, normalized to protein content).
nodes.verbatim_quote: we found significantly higher levels of G6PD in AMIECs than in control cells...Likewise, AMIECs displayed higher levels of G6PD enzyme activity than control cells

strengths: Both Western blotting and enzymatic activity assays provide concordant results.
Protein quantification was normalized to β-actin; activity normalized to protein content.
Triplicate experiments for both measurements.
weaknesses: No downstream PPP metabolite measurements.
Activity was measured in vitro in cell lysates, which may not reflect in situ activity.
required_assumptions: In vitro enzyme activity reflects cellular PPP flux.
evaluation.notes: One of the more rigorously supported evidence claims in the paper.

nodes.label: Flow cytometry with H2DCFDA showed 7/8 AMIECs with significantly higher ROS than…
nodes.claim: Flow cytometry with H2DCFDA showed 7/8 AMIECs with significantly higher ROS than controls; CE-45 was the exception with near-normal ROS and near-normal G6PD protein levels.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Seven out of the 8 AMIECs contained ROS at significantly higher levels than control cells. The one cell line with near-normal ROS levels, CE-45, was the same one displayed normal levels of G6PD protein

strengths: H2DCFDA is a well-established ROS probe used with flow cytometry for quantification.
7/8 lines with elevated ROS provides strong consistency.
CE-45 as an informative exception strengthens the finding.
weaknesses: H2DCFDA can be oxidized by peroxidases and is not specific to a single ROS species.
No specific mitochondrial ROS measurement.
No assessment of ROS source.
required_assumptions: H2DCFDA fluorescence reliably reflects total cellular ROS.

nodes.label: All 8 AMIECs showed increased intracellular reduced glutathione content normaliz…
nodes.claim: All 8 AMIECs showed increased intracellular reduced glutathione content normalized to cellular protein concentration (n=3).
nodes.verbatim_quote: the intracellular concentration of reduced glutathione was increased in all 8 AMIECs

strengths: Enzymatic assay for total GSH is a standard, reliable method.
All 8 AMIEC lines show elevated GSH — the most universal finding in the paper.
Normalization to protein concentration is appropriate.
weaknesses: No measurement of GSSG (oxidized glutathione) to assess the GSH/GSSG ratio, which would better reflect redox status.
n=3 — unclear biological vs. technical replicates.
required_assumptions: Total reduced GSH reflects functional redox buffering capacity.

nodes.label: GC/MS analysis showed significantly higher intracellular cysteine and glutamate …
nodes.claim: GC/MS analysis showed significantly higher intracellular cysteine and glutamate concentrations in all AMIECs compared to controls.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Cysteine and glutamate play important roles in the synthesis of glutathione (GSH) and both had significantly higher concentrations in all AMIECs

strengths: GC/MS is a gold-standard analytical method for metabolite quantification.
Internal standard (Norvaline) was used for normalization.
Consistent across all AMIECs.
weaknesses: Relative quantification rather than absolute quantification was used.
The extraction and derivatization protocol is standard but each step introduces potential variability.
required_assumptions: GC/MS relative quantification with internal standard is reliable for amino acid comparison.

nodes.label: GC/MS revealed higher intracellular content of most amino acids in AMIECs except…
nodes.claim: GC/MS revealed higher intracellular content of most amino acids in AMIECs except glycine, alanine, histidine, and proline; CE45 displayed the amino acid profile most resembling controls.
nodes.verbatim_quote: The results disclosed a higher intracellular content of all amino acids determined, with the exception of glycine, alanine, histidine, and proline. Among AMIECs, CE45 displayed the intracellular amino acid profile most resembling that of control HCAECs

strengths: Comprehensive amino acid profiling by GC/MS.
Both elevated and non-elevated amino acids are reported, demonstrating selectivity rather than global increase.
CE45 as the most control-like cell line is consistent with other observations.
weaknesses: No statistical testing for individual amino acids is described in this claim.
The exceptions (glycine, alanine, histidine, proline) are noted but not discussed mechanistically.
alternative_interpretations: Broadly elevated amino acids could reflect increased protein catabolism or increased amino acid import rather than specific metabolic reprogramming.
required_assumptions: Intracellular amino acid pools reflect metabolic pathway activities.

nodes.label: UCP1 knockout caused vascular dysfunction, atherogenesis, and NLRP3 inflammasome…
nodes.claim: UCP1 knockout caused vascular dysfunction, atherogenesis, and NLRP3 inflammasome activation, which was relieved by UCP1 re-expression or treatment with chemical uncouplers (Gu et al., 2021).
nodes.verbatim_quote: knockout of the uncoupling protein UCP1 caused vascular dysfunction, atherogenesis, and NLRP3 inflammasome activation and IL1-β-dependent inflammation, relieved by re-expression of UCP1 or treatment of animals with chemical uncouplers

strengths: Cites a specific published study (Gu et al., 2021) with relevant in vivo data.
The precedent of UCP1 knockout causing vascular dysfunction and rescue by uncouplers directly supports the therapeutic hypothesis.
weaknesses: This is evidence from an animal model, not from the current study or human cells.
UCP1 knockout is a genetic model, not equivalent to the metabolic phenotype observed in AMIECs.
Translation from animal models to human disease is uncertain.
The referenced study addresses vascular dysfunction broadly, not specifically AMI-derived endothelial cells.
alternative_interpretations: UCP1 knockout may cause vascular dysfunction through mechanisms distinct from those operating in AMIECs.
The NLRP3 inflammasome/IL-1β pathway may be more relevant than uncoupling per se.
required_assumptions: Animal model results are translatable to human AMI patient-derived endothelial cells.
The mechanism of vascular dysfunction in UCP1 knockout is analogous to that in AMIECs.
evaluation.notes: This is cited literature evidence rather than evidence generated in the current study. It supports the plausibility of the therapeutic hypothesis but does not validate it.

summary.overall_assessment: The paper presents 52 claims with mixed overall support (28 high, 6 low).
